title: Build your first SysML v2 model
introduction: Based on Steve’s recorded walkthrough. Start in an empty practice project. You will create a Model package, two part usages and a connection, then create a view and edit multiplicity. The tour guides your clicks; you make the model changes.

steps.title: Start with an empty project
steps.content: Use a new practice project with no package called Model. If you still need to create a project, exit this tour and follow the project-creation Scribe exercise in this catalogue. Return here once the project is open.

steps.title: Add a model element
steps.content: Click the plus icon above the browser to open Add element. We will create a package first.

steps.title: Choose Package
steps.content: Select the Package tile. A package groups related elements in a namespace; it is not a physical part of the system.

steps.title: Name the package
steps.content: Enter Model as the declared name. Leave Owner empty so this package is created at the top level of this practice model.

steps.title: Create the package
steps.content: Check the name and empty Owner field, then click Add. The Model package will appear in the browser.

steps.title: Save the package
steps.content: Click Save in the project toolbar. As in your walkthrough, saving and committing changes are separate actions. Continue when the save completes.

steps.title: Add children to Model
steps.content: Open the three-dot menu on the Model row, then choose Create child element. This makes Model the owner of the elements you create.

steps.title: Use textual specifications
steps.content: Turn on Add element using textual specifications. RSE can create several elements from SysML v2 text in one operation.

steps.title: Create two parts and a connection
steps.content:
Enter the text below in the SysML v2 element text field. These are part usages named hello and world. A part definition would use part def. The connect statement creates a connection between the usages; it does not define a flow.
Check that Owner is Model, then click Add in the application dialog. Next becomes available after the dialog closes.

steps.title: Check the new elements
steps.content: Expand Model if necessary to see hello and world in the browser. The connection is also owned by Model. The tour continues when both parts are visible. If you cancelled Add element, reopen Create child element and finish adding the SysML text.

steps.title: Create a view
steps.content: Open the Model row menu and choose Populate to a new view. The view will display the existing elements; it does not create duplicate parts.

steps.title: Choose a General view
steps.content: In the populate dialog, choose General and click Populate. Keep Model as the owner and include its contents. RSE should open the new view.

steps.title: Explore the diagram palette
steps.content: Expand the palette using its arrow if it is collapsed. Its sections group packages, definitions, usages, relationships and connectors. Hover over an icon to see its meaning.

steps.title: Select hello
steps.content: Click the hello part on the diagram or in the browser. Its properties appear on the right. A symbol in a view refers to a model element.

steps.title: Set multiplicity to 2
steps.content: In Essential properties, enter 2 in Cardinality, then click Apply. This means exactly two values of this part usage. RSE may still draw one symbol representing that usage.

steps.title: Explore the other properties
steps.content: Inspect Other properties, Owned relationships, References and Metadata. These describe different aspects of the selected element. Return to Essential when finished.

steps.title: Find world with search
steps.content: Open project search, enter world and choose the result. Its browser menu offers Find in views so you can locate the element in a diagram.

steps.title: Save your first model
steps.content: Save the project. You have organised elements in a package, created two part usages and a connection, viewed them graphically and explored multiplicity. Finish returns you to training.
